title: Durable scheduling: readiness, ownership, retry, cancellation
note: A scheduler's enforcement points are the ones that decide whether work runs at all, who owns it, and what happens when it does not succeed. Each mutation here removes one. The sharpest are N3 (a failed dependency stops blocking, so dependents wait forever on work nobody will do), N7 (a stale lease may report success, so a worker back from the dead overwrites the outcome someone else produced) and N12 (a verification failure becomes retryable, which is how a flaky pass is eventually obtained).
